title: Controlled dynamics of a multi-component discrete-time quantum walker
abstract: We investigate a discrete-time quantum walk of a three-component quantum particle on a one-dimensional lattice. As coin operators, we employ parameterized rotations generated by the Gell-Mann matrices, which enable systematic tuning of the couplings between the internal components. We analyze how these couplings influence and control the dynamics by systematically exploring the position-space probability distribution across a broad region of the parameter space. To quantify the impact of different inter-component couplings, we further examine the ratio of the mean position to the variance in each half of the lattice. Our results indicates that the system supports a rich variety of transport regimes, ranging from nearly symmetric, rapidly spreading walks to strongly anisotropic dynamics with partial localization. This framework thus provides a new avenue for engineering targeted spreading and trapping behavior in multicomponent discrete-time quantum walks.
summary: The paper investigates a three-component quantum walker whose dynamics are controlled by an SU(3) coin operator. By tuning the coupling parameters, researchers map out a complex phase diagram that allows for engineering specific transport behaviors. This demonstrates a powerful method to control spreading and localization in multi-component quantum systems.
main_problem: The study aims to systematically tune and control the transport properties of a multi-component quantum walker by manipulating pairwise couplings within its coin operator.
main_result: The system exhibits a rich phase diagram in parameter space, allowing for engineered regimes ranging from rapid ballistic spreading to strongly anisotropic dynamics with partial localization.
method: Analysis involves simulating the time evolution of the state using an SU(3) coin operator and quantifying transport via spatio-temporal probability distributions and side-resolved mean/variance ratios.
model_or_system: The model is a discrete-time quantum walk of a three-component particle (qutrit) on a 1D lattice. The evolution is governed by $U = S C(\alpha,  eta, \gamma)$, where the coin operator $C$ uses Gell-Mann matrices to couple internal components.
key_observables: Spatio-temporal probability distribution $P(x, t)$; ballistic spreading rate $m( eta, \gamma)$; side-resolved mean position ratios ($R_X$) and variance ratios ($R_\sigma$).
important_parameters: The coupling parameters $(\alpha,  eta, \gamma)$, particularly exploring regimes near $ eta \sim\pm\pi/2$ and $\gamma \sim\pm\pi/2$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the walk remains ballistic across all tested parameter regimes; a fixed initial state $|\Psi(0)angle =  rac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|Rangle + |Bangle) \otimes |0angle$ is used.

paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the dynamics by first defining the controlled Hamiltonian/evolution operator, then applying diagnostics like $\sigma(t)$ and side-resolved ratios to map out how varying $( eta, \gamma)$ controls transport regimes in a structured phase diagram.
why_interesting: This work provides a general framework for engineering quantum transport using internal degrees of freedom (the qutrit components) rather than relying solely on external lattice geometry or topological constraints.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (Top Row): The probability distribution P(x, t) for the three–state walk for two representative choices of the SU(3) coin parameters (β, γ), as indicated in each panel. The walker is initially localized at the origin with the coin in equal superposition of |R⟩and |B⟩as given by Eq. (9). The color scale shows the total probability at each lattice site. The red and the blue lines indicate the expectation value of the probability distributions XL and XR. (Bottom Left): The time evolution of σ(t) for four representative pairs of couplings (β, γ). (Bottom Right): slope m(β, γ) that is calculated from the long-time evolution over the full range of couplings β and γ.

FIG. 2. The probability P(x, t) of finding the walker at lattice site x at fixed time t = 100 and different coupling angle β going from −π to π. (Top Row): fixed values of γ = 0, π/4, π/3 and π/2. (Bottom Row): fixed ratios γ/β = 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, and 1. The dynamics is symmetric under the swap β →γ, except for the mirror reflection about x = 0.

FIG. 3. Ratio of variances Rσ = σ2 R/σ2 L (Left) and the mean- position RX = −XR/XL (Right) between the right and left halves of the lattice at fixed evolution time t = 500 as a function of the coin parameters (β, γ). The decoupling limit β = γ = 0 is nearly symmetric, while finite couplings generate extended regions of pronounced directional bias, organized along smooth curves in parameter space.
